public_rationale: The statement is hedged and framed as a general pattern. It begins "Across the board, the message seems to be fairly simple", so it reports the impression his own survey of projects gave him. It is not a firm claim about the industry. He does not say whether "build" means the first phase or the whole campus. He gives no size bands and no schedule baseline for "less likely to get completed on schedule." Testing it would mean adding measurement choices he did not make. The rules allow a plain reading only for firm language. As context only: on 2025-11-10, Epoch AI reported that for the large US AI sites it tracks that broke ground in the past three years, the time from starting construction to 1 GW of total facility power ranges from 1 to 3.6 years. The same note says xAI was projecting 12 months for Colossus 2. It also says the first gigawatt-scale sites were expected to come online in early 2026, so these figures include expected milestones, not only completed ones.
limitations: The Epoch AI context covers only the largest US AI data center campuses and one milestone, 1 GW of total facility power.
